text: The 2019–20 Primeira Liga, also known as Liga NOS due to sponsorship, marked the 86th season of Portugal's top professional football league. The season began on 9 August 2019 and concluded on 26 July 2020. Benfica were the defending champions, having won their 37th league title in the prior season. Paços de Ferreira and Famalicão were promoted from the 2018–19 LigaPro, while Gil Vicente were promoted directly from the 2018–19 Campeonato de Portugal by court decision. These three teams replaced Chaves, Nacional, and Feirense, who were relegated to the 2019–20 LigaPro. A total of eighteen teams competed: the top fifteen from the previous season, the two promoted from LigaPro, and one promoted from the third-tier Campeonato de Portugal. Paços de Ferreira returned to the top division one season after being relegated, while Famalicão secured their return after a 25-year absence; Gil Vicente, who had been relegated in the 2018–19 season, were reinstated by court decision five years after their last participation. On 12 March 2020, the Liga Portuguesa de Futebol Profissional (LPFP) suspended the Primeira Liga due to the COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal. Following government approval, the league resumed on 3 June with the remaining ten matchdays played behind closed doors. On 15 July 2020, Porto won their 29th league title with two matches remaining after defeating Sporting CP 2–0 at home. After the season ended, Desportivo das Aves and Portimonense were relegated to the 2020–21 LigaPro, but two days later, both Desportivo das Aves and Vitória de Setubal were relegated to the 2020–21 Campeonato de Portugal by LPFP decision after failing to meet registration requirements. On 10 March 2020, the LPFP announced that matchday 24 (6–8 March) fixtures would be played behind closed doors due to government restrictions on events with more than 5,000 people in open spaces or more than 1,000 participants in closed settings, effective until 3 April. Two days later, the LPFP suspended both the Primeira Liga and LigaPro due to the pandemic, following the Portuguese Football Federation's suspension of non-professional competitions and an emergency meeting involving the Sindicato dos Jogadores Profissionais de Futebol (SJPF), LPFP, and FPF, with the SJPF warning of aggravated financial losses in case of infection. LPFP president Pedro Proença met with club presidents to assess the impact and announced a COVID-19 economic support plan and the creation of an Economic Impact Monitoring Group to support clubs. The FPF also established a €1 million credit line for non-professional clubs. On 28 April, Prime Minister António Costa met with the presidents of the "Big Three" clubs (Benfica, Sporting CP, FC Porto), the FPF, and LPFP to discuss football's return, which caused controversy as clubs like Braga and Vitória de Guimarães felt excluded. On 11 May, several teams had players test positive for COVID-19, including a player from Benfica’s reserve team, and three players from Famalicão, Moreirense, and Vitória de Guimarães were sent home and isolated. On 20 May, LPFP president Pedro Proença proposed that matches be broadcast on free-to-air RTP instead of pay TV, supported by the Portuguese government, but the proposal sparked controversy with NOS and other sponsors, including Benfica and Porto, leading to rumors of Proença being forced out, which he later denied. Benfica subsequently left the LPFP board due to the controversy. On 14 May, following a meeting of clubs, five substitutions were permitted under IFAB’s temporary allowance, proposed by FIFA to reduce fixture congestion. On 22 May, the LPFP confirmed the league would resume on 3 June. On 27 May, an assistant referee for a Benfica vs. Marítimo match tested positive and was replaced. On 30 May, the LPFP approved a plan to resume the league, but Marítimo refused the five-substitution rule; the rule was eventually accepted on 8 June by the LPFP despite the refusal. The table of team positions reflects results after each week, with postponed matches not included in their original scheduled round but added to the subsequent full round. Annual awards were announced on 29 August 2020.
